blockingIssues.description: When the final public booking-detail URL is opened without an authenticated session or `sr_access` cookie, the page redirects to `/auth/signin?redirectedFrom=/bookings/recover?next=...` rather than preserving the original recovery entrypoint with the tokenized/manage-link context. After successful recovery strips the token from the final URL, any later revisit to `/bookings/[bookingId]` cannot re-enter the canonical `/bookings/recover` flow, which breaks the required cookie-backed continuation and deterministic entitled public booking path contract.

The feature requires deprecated guest/public thank-you aliases to resolve to the right canonical destinations, but this feature only changed receipt messaging/tests and left the generic /guest/thank-you alias redirecting to /guest/dashboard without any new coverage or evidence tying that destination to a completed booking/receipt flow. The handoff claims the thank-you aliases already routed correctly, yet the reviewed commit 98fc48a7 contains no validation of /guest/thank-you, so the feature is incomplete against its alias-canonicalization requirement.

The unauthenticated public booking-detail test expects `/auth/signin?redirectedFrom=/bookings/:id`, but the actual route redirects through the canonical recovery entrypoint (`withRedirectedFrom('/auth/signin', '/bookings/recover?next=...')`). This locks in behavior that contradicts the route's token/recovery normalization contract and the feature's requirement to preserve manage-route canonicalization via recovery before the final destination.

The shared-detail reuse test only asserts that rendering the guest booking detail page returns a truthy React node. It never verifies that the page actually reuses the shared public/guest booking detail model or forwards the correct route-specific props, so the central requirement to keep public and guest booking detail on one shared detail model remains effectively unreviewed.
